en.name: Yerba mate
en.summary: Sealed and kept cool and dry, yerba mate keeps about 2 years from purchase, and 6–12 months once opened. No food safety agency publishes a figure for yerba, so both numbers are borrowed wholesale from loose leaf tea — the same kind of dried, cured leaf, handled the same way.
en.pantry: Sealed, cool, dark and dry — a cupboard, not the counter beside the kettle — for about 2 years from purchase, and 6–12 months after opening. Good yerba is aged for months or years before it is sold, so it is already a stable dried leaf; what ruins it is damp and light. Keep the bag clipped or decant it into a tin. Once opened it loses aroma steadily and the fine dust settles to the bottom, so buy the size you will actually drink. Yerba that smells of hay and nothing else, or of the cupboard it lived in, is stale rather than unsafe.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for yerba mate, and the fridge is a poor home for it. Yerba is hygroscopic, so a cold bag opened in a warm room collects condensation, and it will also take up the smell of everything else in there. A sealed opaque tin in a dry cupboard is what the figures above assume.
en.freezer: Do not freeze it. Yerba is strongly hygroscopic and a freezer means condensation every time you open the bag, which is the one thing that genuinely spoils it. There is no freezer timeline and there should not be one. A gourd is a different matter entirely: a wet calabash left with damp yerba in it grows mould within a day, so empty and dry it after every session.
en.thawing: Not applicable — yerba mate should not be frozen.
spoilage: A smell of hay, dust or the cupboard rather than the green, grassy note of fresh yerba.
Leaves that feel damp or have clumped together.
Visible mould, which usually means the bag or the gourd got wet.
A brew that tastes flat and thin where it used to be bracing.
tips: Decant into an airtight tin; the paper bag is not a moisture barrier.
Buy the size you will drink within a year of opening.
Empty and dry the gourd after every session — that is where mould actually appears.
Keep it away from the kettle; steam is what ruins a bag of yerba.

faq.q: How long does yerba mate keep?
faq.a: About 2 years from purchase while sealed, and 6–12 months once opened. These figures are read across from loose leaf tea; no agency publishes one for yerba.
No. It is hygroscopic, and a freezer means condensation every time the bag is opened, which is exactly what ruins it.
It goes stale rather than unsafe — flat, hay-like, thin in the cup. Mould is a real problem in a damp gourd, not in a dry bag.

zh.name: 馬黛茶
zh.summary: 密封、放在陰涼乾燥處，馬黛茶自購買日起大約可放 2 年，開封後 6～12 個月。沒有任何食品安全機關為它公布數字，所以這兩個都是整套從散裝茶葉那邊借來的——同樣是乾燥熟成的葉子，處理方式也一樣。
zh.pantry: 密封、陰涼、避光、乾燥——收在櫃子裡，不要放在熱水壺旁的檯面上——自購買日起約 2 年，開封後 6～12 個月。好的馬黛茶在出貨前已經熟成數月甚至數年，本來就是穩定的乾葉；毀掉它的是潮濕與光線。請把袋口夾好，或倒進鐵罐。開封後香氣會持續流失、細粉也會沉到袋底，所以買你真的喝得完的份量。聞起來只剩乾草味、或一股櫃子味的馬黛茶，是走味而不是不安全。
zh.fridge: 馬黛茶沒有公布的冷藏期限，而冰箱對它來說是個糟糕的歸宿。馬黛很會吸濕，冰過的袋子在溫暖房間打開就會結露；而且它也會把冰箱裡所有味道都吸過來。上面那些數字預設的條件，是不透光的密封鐵罐放在乾燥櫥櫃裡。
zh.freezer: 不要冷凍。馬黛極為吸濕，而冷凍代表每次開袋都結露一次，而那正是真正會毀掉它的事。它沒有冷凍的期限數據，也不該有。葫蘆杯則是完全另一回事：濕葫蘆裡留著濕馬黛，一天之內就會長霉，所以每次喝完都要倒乾淨、晾乾。
zh.thawing: 不適用——馬黛茶不應冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來是乾草味、灰塵味或櫃子味，而不是新鮮馬黛那股青草氣。
葉子摸起來潮濕，或黏成一團。
看得到霉，通常代表袋子或葫蘆杯進了水。
沖出來平淡單薄，不再有原本那股勁道。
tips: 倒進氣密鐵罐；紙袋擋不住水氣。
買開封後一年內喝得完的份量。
每次喝完都把葫蘆杯倒乾淨、晾乾——霉真正出現的地方在那裡。
遠離熱水壺；毀掉一袋馬黛的就是蒸氣。

faq.a: 密封自購買日起約 2 年，開封後 6～12 個月。這些數字是比照散裝茶葉而來，沒有機關公布馬黛茶的期限。
不行。它很會吸濕，冷凍代表每次開袋都結露，而那正是毀掉它的原因。
它是走味而不是變得不安全——平淡、乾草味、沖出來很薄。發霉是潮濕葫蘆杯的問題，不是乾燥袋子的問題。
